attempts.summary: Configured node1 (SONiC) as an inter-VLAN router between node2 and node3. node1's eth1 was assigned 192.168.11.1/24 facing node2 (192.168.11.2/24) and eth2 was assigned 192.168.12.1/24 facing node3 (192.168.12.2/24), with IPv4 forwarding enabled globally and per-interface. Static routes were added on node2 (to 192.168.12.0/24 via node1) and node3 (to 192.168.11.0/24 via node1). Verified node2 and node3 can ping each other across the VLAN boundary with TTL=63, proving traffic is routed through node1. All configuration was persisted (SONiC via /etc/network/interfaces.d and /etc/sysctl.d; Alpine via /etc/network/interfaces with an `up ip route` hook). Then ran the mandatory restart protocol: captured healthy baselines (boot_id, interface/route state, ping tests) on all three nodes, restarted node2, node3, and node1 sequentially (one at a time), polled each until it came back, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and re-verified persisted routing config and end-to-end cross-VLAN ping after every restart, including after node1 (the router) came back last.
